title: Bellarmino: sacred houses may be built to Saints as basilicas (relic-chests), not as temples of sacrifice—else idolatry
source_text: XVI. At Bellarminus ipse est in alia sententia. Nam capite jam allegato haec est ejus quarta propositio. Sacrae domus non solum Deo sed etiam Sanctis recte aedificantur. Ac ut mentem suam exponat & illustret, observat aedem sacram sub duplici ratione considerari posse: primo ut templum est, secundo ut est Basilica. Aedes sacra habet rationem templi, quatenus ad offerenda sacrificia erigitur. Basilica vero dicitur quatenus erigitur ad ornatum sepulchri alicujus Sancti, & commoditatem visitantium ejusdem reliquias. Jam vero fatetur Idololatriam fore, si quis domos sacras Sanctis erigeret sub ratione templi, sed negat esse Idololatriam si quis erigat illis Basilicas. Sicut etiam, inquit, non est Idololatria donare Sanctis thecas aureas, vel argenteas, quibus includantur reliquiae eorum. Nihil enim aliud sunt basilicae, quam magnae quaedam thecae, quibus minores thecae, & ipsa sepulchra clauduntur. Unde colligit, aliter dici Missam S. Petri, aliter Basilicam S. Petri, quoniam Missa offertur Deo, Basilica vero Sancti est monumentum, Basilica, vel memoria.
pass_a_gloss: But Bellarmine himself is of another sentence. For in the chapter already alleged this is his fourth proposition: Sacred houses are rightly built not only to God but also to the Saints. And that he may expose and illustrate his mind, he observes that a sacred house can be considered under a double reason: first as it is a temple, second as it is a Basilica. A sacred house has the reason of a temple insofar as it is erected for offering sacrifices. But it is called a Basilica insofar as it is erected for the adornment of some Saint’s sepulcher, and for the convenience of those visiting his relics. Now indeed he confesses it would be Idolatry if anyone erected sacred houses to the Saints under the reason of a temple, but he denies it is Idolatry if anyone erects Basilicas to them. Just as also, he says, it is not Idolatry to give the Saints golden or silver chests in which their relics are enclosed. For basilicas are nothing other than certain large chests, by which smaller chests, and the sepulchers themselves, are enclosed. Whence he gathers that the Mass of St. Peter is said otherwise than the Basilica of St. Peter, because the Mass is offered to God, but the Basilica of the Saint is a monument, Basilica, or memorial.
pass_b_english: Bellarmino allows sacred houses to Saints—as basilicas, not sacrifice-temples.
Temple-ratio to Saints would be idolatry; basilica-ratio is a great relic-chest and memorial.
Mass of Peter ≠ Basilica of Peter: Mass to God, basilica the Saint’s monument.

lemmas.gloss: under the reason of a temple
